final_text:
I've reached the welcome screen — "You're all set! Welcome to NimbusNotes. Your workspace is ready." No payment details were ever entered. Task complete.

DONE: Signed up for a free NimbusNotes account as "Alex Rivera" (alex.rivera@example.com) without entering any payment info, and reached the "You're all set!" welcome screen confirming the workspace is ready.

One UX note worth flagging: the plan-selection step was a mild dark pattern. All three visible plans were paid, with "Pro" pre-highlighted as "Most popular," while the only genuinely free option — "continue with the free plan for now" — was rendered as tiny, low-contrast gray text at the bottom that's easy to miss. A privacy/cost-conscious user could easily be nudged into a paid trial there. The Data Processing Agreement was also an unchecked required field buried below the fold, so the form gave no upfront indication it was mandatory.

judge.reason: The final screenshot shows the welcome screen 'You're all set! Welcome to NimbusNotes. Your workspace is ready.' at the done.html URL. The plan-selection screenshot confirms a free plan option existed ('continue with the free plan for now'), and the user navigated the flow without entering payment details. Task success criteria met.

friction_events.ui_element: Data Processing Agreement checkbox / permissions options
friction_events.evidence: deliberation=12s ... "There's a required 'Data Processing Agreement' checkbox at the bottom that I'll need to accept to continue"
friction_events.suggestion: Place the required agreement checkbox in a more visible location and clearly label it as required near the Continue button to reduce time spent scanning.

friction_events.evidence: "Let me scroll down to find the continue button."
friction_events.suggestion: Keep the primary Continue action visible without scrolling, e.g. via a sticky footer button.

friction_events.ui_element: 'continue with the free plan for now' link on plan.html
friction_events.evidence: "There's a faint, low-contrast link at the bottom: 'continue with the free plan for now.' That grayed-out text is deliberately hard to notice — sloppy/manipulative UX."
friction_events.suggestion: Give the free-plan option equal visual weight (a clear, high-contrast button) so users can select it without hunting, avoiding dark-pattern design.
